project.description: Renders the env files for the selected PIC-SURE services for one target stack from the shared .tftpl templates and uploads them to S3. The .tftpl is the file people edit: pull it with Download PIC-SURE Configuration Template, change it, and push it back with Upload PIC-SURE Configuration Template. PICSURE_APPLICATION_TOKEN, QUERY_SERVICE_INTERNAL_TOKEN and AGGREGATE_OBFUSCATION_SALT are read back out of the env files currently rendered for the stack and reused, so re-rendering one service no longer rotates the values the other two are still running with. LOGGING_API_KEY is read back out of the rendered logging.env the same way, but that object carries no stack segment, so a key minted here reaches the live stack too: a first render, where the object does not exist yet, mints one and requires RENDER_LOGGING, RENDER_GATEWAY and RENDER_VISUALIZATION all true, while an existing logging.env holding a blank key aborts and refers you to the rotation job. ROTATE_SHARED_SECRETS mints new values for all four instead; it is one switch with no partial states, requiring RENDER_GATEWAY, RENDER_OPERATIONS, RENDER_QUERY, RENDER_LOGGING and RENDER_VISUALIZATION all true, and all five services must be redeployed afterwards. picsure-dictionary's DATASOURCE_URL and DATASOURCE_USERNAME are read back out of the rendered picsure-dictionary.env and can never be generated: a run that cannot read them back stops. One logging service and one dictionary service serve every stack, so neither of those two objects carries a stack segment.

hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.description: Render and upload the open HPDS env file

hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.name: RENDER_VISUALIZATION
hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.description: Render and upload the visualization env file

hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.name: RENDER_LOGGING

DATASOURCE_URL and DATASOURCE_USERNAME must already exist in the rendered object; this job cannot generate them.

hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.name: ROTATE_SHARED_SECRETS
hudson.model.BooleanParameterDefinition.description: Mint new values for PICSURE_APPLICATION_TOKEN, QUERY_SERVICE_INTERNAL_TOKEN, AGGREGATE_OBFUSCATION_SALT and LOGGING_API_KEY instead of reusing the rendered ones. One switch over all four, with no partial states: it requires RENDER_GATEWAY, RENDER_OPERATIONS, RENDER_QUERY, RENDER_LOGGING and RENDER_VISUALIZATION all true, and all five services must be redeployed afterwards.

hudson.tasks.Shell.command:
#!/bin/bash set -euo pipefail
# Source folder containing the scripts source_scripts_folder="${JENKINS_HOME}/workspace/Bash_Functions/"
# Iterate through the files in the folder and source them shopt -s nullglob for script_file in "$source_scripts_folder"*.sh; do chmod +x "$script_file" if [ -f "$script_file" ] && [ -x "$script_file" ]; then echo "sourcing $script_file" source "$script_file" fi done shopt -u nullglob
for required_function in assume_role reset_role fetch_secret extract_field initialize_shared_db_config get_token_by_uuid unset_shared_db_config; do if ! command -v "$required_function" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "Error: required function '$required_function' was not loaded from $source_scripts_folder." >&2 echo "Run the Bash_Functions job, then re-run this job." >&2 exit 1 fi done
: "${TARGET_STACK:?TARGET_STACK is required}" : "${stack_s3_bucket:?stack_s3_bucket is required}"
render_gateway="${RENDER_GATEWAY:-false}" render_operations="${RENDER_OPERATIONS:-false}" render_query="${RENDER_QUERY:-false}" render_auth_hpds="${RENDER_AUTH_HPDS:-false}" render_open_hpds="${RENDER_OPEN_HPDS:-false}" render_visualization="${RENDER_VISUALIZATION:-false}" render_logging="${RENDER_LOGGING:-false}" render_dictionary="${RENDER_DICTIONARY:-false}" rotate_shared_secrets="${ROTATE_SHARED_SECRETS:-false}"
if [ "$render_gateway" != "true" ] && [ "$render_operations" != "true" ] && [ "$render_query" != "true" ] && [ "$render_auth_hpds" != "true" ] && [ "$render_open_hpds" != "true" ] && [ "$render_visualization" != "true" ] && [ "$render_logging" != "true" ] && [ "$render_dictionary" != "true" ]; then echo "Error: no service was selected to render." >&2 echo "Set at least one of RENDER_GATEWAY, RENDER_OPERATIONS, RENDER_QUERY, RENDER_AUTH_HPDS, RENDER_OPEN_HPDS, RENDER_VISUALIZATION, RENDER_LOGGING or RENDER_DICTIONARY to true, then re-run this job." >&2 exit 1 fi
render_services=false if [ "$render_gateway" = "true" ] || [ "$render_operations" = "true" ] || [ "$render_query" = "true" ]; then render_services=true fi
all_picsure_services_selected=false if [ "$render_gateway" = "true" ] && [ "$render_operations" = "true" ] && [ "$render_query" = "true" ]; then all_picsure_services_selected=true fi
all_logging_consumers_selected=false if [ "$render_logging" = "true" ] && [ "$render_gateway" = "true" ] && [ "$render_visualization" = "true" ]; then all_logging_consumers_selected=true fi
all_shared_secret_consumers_selected=false if [ "$all_picsure_services_selected" = "true" ] && [ "$all_logging_consumers_selected" = "true" ]; then all_shared_secret_consumers_selected=true fi
# PICSURE_APPLICATION_TOKEN, QUERY_SERVICE_INTERNAL_TOKEN and AGGREGATE_OBFUSCATION_SALT are # shared by the gateway, operations and query services, and LOGGING_API_KEY is shared by # pic-sure-logging, the gateway and the visualization service. Changing any of them while only # some of that value's consumers re-render leaves the rest holding the old one: # InternalTokenFilter answers the stale token with 403 and the gateway flattens that into an # opaque 500 on query downloads, and pic-sure-logging answers a stale key with 401 while the # logging client drops the event. Rotation is one switch over all four values, so it needs the # union of their consumers -- all five services. if [ "$rotate_shared_secrets" = "true" ] && [ "$all_shared_secret_consumers_selected" != "true" ]; then echo "Error: ROTATE_SHARED_SECRETS changes values that the gateway, operations, query, logging and visualization services share between them." >&2 echo "Set RENDER_GATEWAY, RENDER_OPERATIONS, RENDER_QUERY, RENDER_LOGGING and RENDER_VISUALIZATION all true so the five render together, then redeploy all five." >&2 exit 1 fi
temp_files=() tfstate_dir=""
new_temp_file() { local name_prefix=$1 local created
if ! created=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/${name_prefix}.XXXXXX"); then echo "Error: could not create a temporary file." >&2 return 1 fi temp_files+=("$created") temp_file_path="$created" }
# This render job is stateless (each run inits from empty state), but the local # terraform.tfstate transiently holds live secrets -- DB app-user credentials, the # introspection token, the logging key, the shared service secrets, and the full rendered env # contents. Remove it on exit so it never lingers in the browsable Jenkins workspace. The # read-back copies of the rendered env files carry the same shared secrets and live under # ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}; the same handler removes them, and drops the assumed role. cleanup() { local temp_file
if [ "${#temp_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then for temp_file in "${temp_files[@]}"; do rm -f "$temp_file" 2>/dev/null || true done fi if [ -n "$tfstate_dir" ]; then rm -f "$tfstate_dir"/terraform.tfstate "$tfstate_dir"/terraform.tfstate.backup 2>/dev/null || true fi reset_role } trap cleanup EXIT
assume_role
picsure_token_introspection_token="" if [ "$render_gateway" = "true" ]; then # Get the introspection token from the PSAMA database (same derivation as Teardown # and Rebuild). The token is never echoed: it is a live credential. db_app_user_json=$(fetch_secret "$database_app_user_secret_name") picsure_db_username=$(extract_field "$db_app_user_json" "username") picsure_db_password=$(extract_field "$db_app_user_json" "password") picsure_db_host=$database_host_address
if [ -z "$picsure_db_username" ] || [ -z "$picsure_db_password" ] || [ -z "$picsure_db_host" ]; then echo "Error: One or more required database variables are empty." >&2 exit 1 fi
initialize_shared_db_config "${picsure_db_host%:3306}" "$picsure_db_username" "$picsure_db_password" picsure_token_introspection_token=$(get_token_by_uuid "$application_id_for_base_query") unset_shared_db_config
# Fail closed: rendering with an empty token produces a gateway.env whose introspection # calls PSAMA rejects with 403, which surfaces to users as 502 on authenticated routes. if [ -z "$picsure_token_introspection_token" ]; then echo "Error: no introspection token found for application ${application_id_for_base_query}." >&2 echo "Run the Update PIC-SURE Token Introspection Token job to mint one, then re-run this job." >&2 exit 1 fi fi
cd app-infrastructure/template-renderer tfstate_dir="$PWD"
# Resolve each editable template independently: shared S3 override, then the # checked-out repository version. download_s3_template() { local object_key=$1 local destination=$2 local aws_error local candidate
if ! candidate=$(mktemp "$(dirname "$destination")/.template-download.XXXXXX"); then echo "Error: could not create a temporary template file." >&2 return 2 fi if aws_error=$(aws s3 cp "s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${object_key}" "$candidate" 2>&1 >/dev/null); then if [ ! -s "$candidate" ]; then rm -f "$candidate" echo "Error: s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${object_key} is empty; refusing to use it." >&2 return 2 fi if ! mv "$candidate" "$destination" >/dev/null 2>&1; then rm -f "$candidate" echo "Error: could not promote downloaded template to $destination." >&2 return 2 fi return 0 fi
rm -f "$candidate" case "$aws_error" in *"An error occurred (404)"*|*"An error occurred (NoSuchKey)"*|*"An error occurred (NotFound)"*) return 1 ;; esac
echo "Error: could not read s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${object_key}; refusing to fall back after a non-missing-object AWS error." >&2 return 2 }
resolve_template() { local template_prefix=$1 local template_file=$2 local download_status
if download_s3_template "${template_prefix}/${template_file}" "templates/${template_file}"; then echo "Using shared S3 template for ${template_file}" return 0 else download_status=$? if [ "$download_status" -ne 1 ]; then return "$download_status" fi fi
echo "No S3 template found, using repo version of ${template_file}" }
if [ "$render_gateway" = "true" ]; then resolve_template "configs/gateway/templates" "gateway.env.tftpl" fi
if [ "$render_operations" = "true" ]; then resolve_template "configs/operations/templates" "operations.env.tftpl" fi
if [ "$render_query" = "true" ]; then resolve_template "configs/query/templates" "query.env.tftpl" fi
if [ "$render_auth_hpds" = "true" ]; then resolve_template "configs/hpds/templates" "hpds-auth.env.tftpl" fi
if [ "$render_open_hpds" = "true" ]; then resolve_template "configs/hpds/templates" "hpds-open.env.tftpl" fi
if [ "$render_visualization" = "true" ]; then resolve_template "configs/pic-sure-visualization/templates" "visualization.env.tftpl" fi
if [ "$render_logging" = "true" ]; then resolve_template "configs/pic-sure-logging/templates" "logging.env.tftpl" fi
if [ "$render_dictionary" = "true" ]; then resolve_template "configs/picsure-dictionary/templates" "picsure-dictionary.env.tftpl" fi
# Read one KEY=VALUE out of a rendered env file, anchored at the start of the line, taking # everything after the first '=' as the value. The value is returned in the env_value global # rather than on stdout so that no caller can leak it into the build log. read_env_value() { local env_file=$1 local key=$2 local line
env_value="" while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do case "$line" in "${key}="*) env_value="${line#*=}" return 0 ;; esac done < "$env_file" }
# Decide one shared value from the env files that are currently rendered for this stack. # Exactly one distinct non-empty value across them is reused; none means this run has to # mint one; more than one means the stack is already inconsistent and only the rotation job # can put it right. This replaces the random_password resources that used to mint all three # on every apply: the renderer keeps no Terraform state, so every apply started from empty # state, and re-rendering one service silently rotated the value the other two were running # with. Neither the values nor any comparison of them is ever echoed. resolve_shared_value() { local key=$1 local first_source=${2:-} local second_source=${3:-} local third_source=${4:-} local source_file local candidate local first_value="" local distinct=0
resolved_value="" resolved_origin=generate
for source_file in "$first_source" "$second_source" "$third_source"; do if [ -z "$source_file" ]; then continue fi read_env_value "$source_file" "$key" candidate="$env_value" if [ -z "$candidate" ]; then continue fi if [ "$distinct" -eq 0 ]; then first_value="$candidate" distinct=1 elif [ "$candidate" != "$first_value" ]; then distinct=2 fi done
if [ "$distinct" -gt 1 ]; then echo "Error: the env files rendered for stack ${TARGET_STACK} hold different values for ${key}." >&2 echo "Run the Rotate PIC-SURE Shared Service Secrets job to put one value back across gateway, operations and query, then re-run this job." >&2 return 1 fi
if [ "$distinct" -eq 1 ]; then resolved_value="$first_value" resolved_origin=reused fi }
# Both shapes have to match the random_password resources they replace: the two tokens are # 43 characters of [A-Za-z0-9] and the salt is 32 characters of [a-z0-9]. head closes the # pipe as soon as it has its bytes, so pipefail is dropped for the pipeline only, and the # length is asserted because a short read would otherwise pass silently. generate_shared_token() { generated_value=$(set +o pipefail; LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 43) if [ "${#generated_value}" -ne 43 ]; then echo "Error: generated a ${#generated_value} character token; expected 43." >&2 return 1 fi }
generate_obfuscation_salt() { generated_value=$(set +o pipefail; LC_ALL=C tr -dc 'a-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 32) if [ "${#generated_value}" -ne 32 ]; then echo "Error: generated a ${#generated_value} character salt; expected 32." >&2 return 1 fi }
picsure_application_token="" query_service_internal_token="" aggregate_obfuscation_salt=""
if [ "$render_services" = "true" ]; then gateway_env_copy="" operations_env_copy="" query_env_copy=""
if [ "$rotate_shared_secrets" = "true" ]; then echo "ROTATE_SHARED_SECRETS is true: minting new PICSURE_APPLICATION_TOKEN, QUERY_SERVICE_INTERNAL_TOKEN, AGGREGATE_OBFUSCATION_SALT and LOGGING_API_KEY values. All five of the gateway, operations, query, logging and visualization services must be redeployed afterwards." else for rendered_service in gateway operations query; do rendered_key="configs/${rendered_service}/${TARGET_STACK}/${rendered_service}.env" new_temp_file "${rendered_service}.env" rendered_copy="$temp_file_path" if download_s3_template "$rendered_key" "$rendered_copy"; then echo "Reading shared values back from s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${rendered_key}" case "$rendered_service" in gateway) gateway_env_copy="$rendered_copy" ;; operations) operations_env_copy="$rendered_copy" ;; query) query_env_copy="$rendered_copy" ;; esac else download_status=$? if [ "$download_status" -ne 1 ]; then echo "Error: the message above is from the shared S3 download helper. It was reading the rendered ${rendered_service} env back from s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${rendered_key} to recover the shared values, and there is no template or repository fallback for a rendered env file, so this run stops." >&2 exit "$download_status" fi echo "s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${rendered_key} is not rendered yet" fi done fi
resolve_shared_value "PICSURE_APPLICATION_TOKEN" "$gateway_env_copy" "$operations_env_copy" "$query_env_copy" picsure_application_token="$resolved_value" picsure_application_token_origin="$resolved_origin"
resolve_shared_value "QUERY_SERVICE_INTERNAL_TOKEN" "$gateway_env_copy" "$operations_env_copy" "$query_env_copy" query_service_internal_token="$resolved_value" query_service_internal_token_origin="$resolved_origin"
# The salt lives only in query.env, so only a run that rewrites query.env can change it. # Resolving it on a gateway-only or operations-only render would mint a value nothing # writes and report it as generated, which reads as though the query service now needs a # redeploy. aggregate_obfuscation_salt_origin="not rendered by this run" if [ "$render_query" = "true" ]; then resolve_shared_value "AGGREGATE_OBFUSCATION_SALT" "$query_env_copy" aggregate_obfuscation_salt="$resolved_value" aggregate_obfuscation_salt_origin="$resolved_origin" fi
if [ "$picsure_application_token_origin" = "generate" ] || [ "$query_service_internal_token_origin" = "generate" ]; then if [ "$all_picsure_services_selected" != "true" ]; then echo "Error: nothing rendered for stack ${TARGET_STACK} carries PICSURE_APPLICATION_TOKEN or QUERY_SERVICE_INTERNAL_TOKEN, so this run would have to mint one." >&2 echo "That value is shared by the gateway, operations and query services: set RENDER_GATEWAY, RENDER_OPERATIONS and RENDER_QUERY all true so all three render together on a first render." >&2 exit 1 fi fi
if [ "$picsure_application_token_origin" = "generate" ]; then generate_shared_token picsure_application_token="$generated_value" picsure_application_token_origin=generated fi
if [ "$query_service_internal_token_origin" = "generate" ]; then generate_shared_token query_service_internal_token="$generated_value" query_service_internal_token_origin=generated fi
if [ "$render_query" = "true" ] && [ "$aggregate_obfuscation_salt_origin" = "generate" ]; then generate_obfuscation_salt aggregate_obfuscation_salt="$generated_value" aggregate_obfuscation_salt_origin=generated if [ -n "$query_env_copy" ]; then echo "Warning: query.env for stack ${TARGET_STACK} already existed but carried no AGGREGATE_OBFUSCATION_SALT. A new salt was minted; reported aggregate counts for existing queries will shift." >&2 fi fi
echo "Shared value resolution for stack ${TARGET_STACK}:" echo " PICSURE_APPLICATION_TOKEN: ${picsure_application_token_origin}" echo " QUERY_SERVICE_INTERNAL_TOKEN: ${query_service_internal_token_origin}" echo " AGGREGATE_OBFUSCATION_SALT: ${aggregate_obfuscation_salt_origin}" fi
# LOGGING_API_KEY is presented on POST /audit by the gateway and the visualization service and # checked by pic-sure-logging, so all three env files have to carry the same value. This job # used to read it out of logging.env purely as an input, because that object was # hand-maintained; it renders that object now, so the key is read back out of it exactly as # the shared service secrets are read back out of the rendered service env files. logging.env # carries no stack segment: one logging service serves every stack. The key is never echoed: # it is a live credential. It previously defaulted to the literal string "disabled", which # rendered a gateway.env whose audit events pic-sure-logging rejects with 401 -- silently, # because the logging client logs the failure and drops the event. The two tokens, not the # salt, are the precedent for the gate below: the salt has a single consumer, the query # service, so a run that rewrites query.env can mint one freely, while a minted LOGGING_API_KEY # that reaches only some of its three consumers leaves the rest sending audit events # pic-sure-logging answers with 401. It goes further than those two, though, because logging.env # is the only one of the four shared secrets whose object carries no stack segment: the other # three live under configs/<service>/${TARGET_STACK}/, so minting one touches only the stack # being rendered, while minting this one rewrites the single object every stack reads. BDC runs # blue/green, so during a pipeline run one stack is live while the other is rebuilt, and a new # key would leave the live stack's gateway and visualization presenting the old one. An absent # object is therefore a bootstrap -- nothing running can hold a key from an object that never # existed -- and mints, subject to the all-three gate. A present object with a blank key aborts # instead, whatever the flags are: changing a key a live stack may be using is a both-stacks # operation, which is what ROTATE_SHARED_SECRETS is for, since it redeploys all five consumers # together. logging_api_key="" if [ "$render_logging" = "true" ] || [ "$render_gateway" = "true" ] || [ "$render_visualization" = "true" ]; then logging_env_key="configs/pic-sure-logging/logging.env" logging_env_copy=""
if [ "$rotate_shared_secrets" = "true" ]; then echo "ROTATE_SHARED_SECRETS is true: minting a new LOGGING_API_KEY for pic-sure-logging, gateway and visualization." else new_temp_file "logging.env" logging_env_candidate="$temp_file_path" if download_s3_template "$logging_env_key" "$logging_env_candidate"; then echo "Reading LOGGING_API_KEY back from s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${logging_env_key}" logging_env_copy="$logging_env_candidate" else download_status=$? if [ "$download_status" -ne 1 ]; then echo "Error: the message above is from the shared S3 download helper. It was reading the rendered logging env back from s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${logging_env_key} to recover LOGGING_API_KEY, and there is no template or repository fallback for a rendered env file, so this run stops." >&2 exit "$download_status" fi echo "s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${logging_env_key} is not rendered yet" fi fi
resolve_shared_value "LOGGING_API_KEY" "$logging_env_copy" logging_api_key="$resolved_value" logging_api_key_origin="$resolved_origin"
if [ "$logging_api_key_origin" = "generate" ]; then if [ "$rotate_shared_secrets" != "true" ] && [ -n "$logging_env_copy" ]; then echo "Error: s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${logging_env_key} exists but carries no non-empty LOGGING_API_KEY." >&2 echo "That object has no stack segment -- one logging service serves every stack -- so minting a key here would leave any live stack's gateway and visualization presenting the old one, and pic-sure-logging answers those with 401 while the logging client drops the audit event." >&2 echo "Run the Rotate PIC-SURE Shared Service Secrets job to change this value: that path redeploys all five consumers together, which is what makes a new key safe." >&2 exit 1 fi if [ "$all_logging_consumers_selected" != "true" ]; then echo "Error: nothing is rendered at s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${logging_env_key}, so this run would have to mint LOGGING_API_KEY." >&2 echo "That value is shared by the pic-sure-logging, gateway and visualization services: set RENDER_LOGGING, RENDER_GATEWAY and RENDER_VISUALIZATION all true so all three render together on a first render." >&2 exit 1 fi generate_shared_token logging_api_key="$generated_value" logging_api_key_origin=generated fi
echo "Logging key resolution:" echo " LOGGING_API_KEY: ${logging_api_key_origin}" fi
# DATASOURCE_URL and DATASOURCE_USERNAME are read back and never minted. Unlike the shared # service secrets they are not values this job is free to choose: the URL is the bare host of # a database that already exists and the username is a Secrets Manager secret id whose secret # holds the real username and password. A generated value would render a # picsure-dictionary.env that cannot open a connection at all, so a run that cannot read one # back stops rather than shipping a guess. Both are currently supplied by the container image # rather than by this file -- bdc.Dockerfile promotes them from build arguments to ENV, and the # PIC-SURE Dictionary Image job passes them from parameters of the same names -- so the rendered # object may not carry them yet. That makes stopping more important, not less: podman # --env-file overrides the image ENV, so a blank or guessed value would not leave the working # datasource settings alone, it would take them away. Neither value is echoed, matching how # app_user_secret_name is handled. dictionary_datasource_url="" dictionary_datasource_username="" if [ "$render_dictionary" = "true" ]; then dictionary_env_key="configs/picsure-dictionary/picsure-dictionary.env" dictionary_env_copy="" new_temp_file "picsure-dictionary.env" dictionary_env_candidate="$temp_file_path" if download_s3_template "$dictionary_env_key" "$dictionary_env_candidate"; then echo "Reading the datasource settings back from s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${dictionary_env_key}" dictionary_env_copy="$dictionary_env_candidate" else download_status=$? if [ "$download_status" -ne 1 ]; then echo "Error: the message above is from the shared S3 download helper. It was reading the rendered dictionary env back from s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${dictionary_env_key} to recover DATASOURCE_URL and DATASOURCE_USERNAME, and there is no template or repository fallback for a rendered env file, so this run stops." >&2 exit "$download_status" fi echo "s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${dictionary_env_key} is not rendered yet" fi
for dictionary_key in DATASOURCE_URL DATASOURCE_USERNAME; do env_value="" if [ -n "$dictionary_env_copy" ]; then read_env_value "$dictionary_env_copy" "$dictionary_key" fi if [ -z "$env_value" ]; then echo "Error: s3://${stack_s3_bucket}/${dictionary_env_key} carries no non-empty ${dictionary_key}." >&2 echo "${dictionary_key} names infrastructure that already exists, so this job cannot mint one the way it mints the shared service secrets. The value is currently supplied by the container image: picsure-dictionary's bdc.Dockerfile promotes it to an ENV, and the PIC-SURE Dictionary Image job passes it as a build argument from its own ${dictionary_key} parameter." >&2 echo "Seed that object with the same value the running image was built with, then re-run this job. Rendering picsure-dictionary.env without it would take the setting away rather than leave it alone, because podman --env-file overrides the image ENV." >&2 exit 1 fi case "$dictionary_key" in DATASOURCE_URL) dictionary_datasource_url="$env_value" ;; DATASOURCE_USERNAME) dictionary_datasource_username="$env_value" ;; esac done
echo "Dictionary datasource resolution:" echo " DATASOURCE_URL: read back" echo " DATASOURCE_USERNAME: read back" fi
# Every sensitive value reaches Terraform through the environment. A -var argument would be # readable in the process list of a shared Jenkins agent for the length of the apply. if [ "$render_gateway" = "true" ]; then export TF_VAR_picsure_token_introspection_token="$picsure_token_introspection_token" fi
if [ "$render_logging" = "true" ] || [ "$render_gateway" = "true" ] || [ "$render_visualization" = "true" ]; then export TF_VAR_logging_api_key="$logging_api_key" fi
if [ "$render_services" = "true" ]; then export TF_VAR_picsure_application_token="$picsure_application_token" export TF_VAR_query_service_internal_token="$query_service_internal_token" fi
if [ "$render_operations" = "true" ]; then export TF_VAR_app_user_secret_name="$database_app_user_secret_name" fi
if [ "$render_query" = "true" ]; then export TF_VAR_aggregate_obfuscation_salt="$aggregate_obfuscation_salt" fi
if [ "$render_dictionary" = "true" ]; then export TF_VAR_dictionary_datasource_url="$dictionary_datasource_url" export TF_VAR_dictionary_datasource_username="$dictionary_datasource_username" fi
apply_args=( -auto-approve -input=false -var="stack_s3_bucket=${stack_s3_bucket}" -var="environment_name=${environment_name}" -var="target_stack=${TARGET_STACK}" -var="env_private_dns_name=${env_private_dns_name}" -var="render_gateway=${render_gateway}" -var="render_operations=${render_operations}" -var="render_query=${render_query}" -var="render_auth_hpds=${render_auth_hpds}" -var="render_open_hpds=${render_open_hpds}" -var="render_visualization=${render_visualization}" -var="render_logging=${render_logging}" -var="render_dictionary=${render_dictionary}" )
# include_open_hpds is read only by the gateway template, and its value comes from a Jenkins # global. Passing it on a non-gateway run would still reference that global, and set -u would # abort the run on a controller where the global is unset. The Terraform default is false. if [ "$render_gateway" = "true" ]; then apply_args+=(-var="include_open_hpds=${include_open_hpds}") fi
terraform init -input=false
terraform apply "${apply_args[@]}"
reset_role
